To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) it is impossible to reconstruct the state of the system if more than 50% of the sensors are attacked, (b) the design of a local control loop can help the resilience of the global system and (c) the principle of separation holds for the design of resilient control systems.

(1) we characterize the resilience of the state estimation problem to sensor attacks and we give a new simple formula for the maximum number of detectable attacks; (2) we propose a method to estimate the state in the presence of sensor attacks that has good performance in terms of accuracy; (3) we propose a resilient controller design method that can be used to design controllers resilient to sensor attacks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of designing resilient control loops for linear systems that are subject to attacks on their sensors or actuators.
the design of resilient estimation and control algorithms for cyber-physical systems under sensor and actuator attacks.
the fundamental question of the resilience of control systems against cyber-attacks and with the development of efficient and scalable algorithms for secure estimation and control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a framework to design resilient control systems that are secure, robust and resilient against cyber attacks.
the design of secure control loops can improve the resilience to attacks and can be achieved with a simple design procedure that can be implemented in real time.
the design of secure control systems is a difficult and complex problem that requires a multidisciplinary approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the foundations for secure estimation and control in the presence of attacks.

it is impossible for a system to resist more than half the sensor attacks, but that the design of secure local control loops can improve the robustness of the system to attacks and that the design problem can be decomposed in a principled way into the design of secure estimators and secure controllers.

the paper proposes a new simple characterization for the maximum number of sensor attacks that can be tolerated, proposes a novel algorithm that can reconstruct the state accurately and proposes a novel resilient control design methodology that can be applied to any linear system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of secure feedback control systems is feasible, even when the number of attacks exceeds half the number of sensors.
it is possible to design secure control systems that are resilient against attacks on sensors and actuators.
a secure estimation algorithm is necessary but not sufficient to ensure the security of a cyber-physical system.
